answer: A lasting defence is a seasonal community exchange. Each newcomer is seconded to a foreign community for one season to forge real working ties there: it must complete checkable tasks for strangers, and only the host community's public endorsement grants standing. Hosts rotate by lottery, so a farm operator cannot plant fakes in friendly territory. Like crystal, trust grows slowly and visibly, layer by layer, and any fable of fake productivity shatters when the host's independent audit finds no real work. Endorsements expire each season, so standing must be re-earned abroad.
